title: Unmodified OMP 18.4.0 keeps one NInfer session across graceful restarts on both v0.8.7 runtimes
question: v0.8.7 changes how both runtimes keep checkpoints: a session's checkpoint stays on its stored, compacted lineage, and quota reclamation takes short sessions' checkpoints first. Does the upstream OMP 18.4.0 release binary, configured only by each documented route's fragment and this release's fail-closed config, still keep one durable session across graceful server restarts on the v0.6.13 RTX 5090 and v0.6.10 RTX 4090 runtimes, as it did on v0.8.4's (EXP-067)?
answer: Yes on both lanes. In all three scenarios - one OMP process across a restart, a new process with the server up, and a new process after a restart - OMP 18.4.0 recalled both seeded facts under one OMP session id, no graceful stop refused a save, and every turn after the seed reused the session's cache: 7,282-7,402 cached tokens with the first token in 0.12-0.23 s on the RTX 5090 and 7,284-7,646 in 0.18-0.40 s on the RTX 4090, where each seed prefilled about 7.3K tokens from root in 2.23 s and 3.47 s. After the second restart each lane restored the session's checkpoint on the new process's first request, which named no response id.

method.probe: scripts/stock_omp_session_proof.py with the EXP-053/EXP-067 scenarios unchanged (b4669d1 only added an optional event observer for scripts/omp_long_session_proof.py): RPC mode with PI_OPENAI_STATEFUL=1 and an isolated HOME holding the route's documented models.yml and this release's fail-closed config.yml verbatim (async compaction on, one request in flight per NInfer provider); thinking low; synthetic prompts. Per-turn cache figures are the servers' own request_done records for the proof's requests.
method.why: EXP-067 proved stock-client durability on v0.8.4's runtimes, and v0.8.5-v0.8.6 carried it with unchanged runtimes. v0.8.7 changes both runtimes' checkpoint lineage and reclamation, so the proof reruns on each v0.8.7 runtime before the release claims it.

limits: One run per lane with one OMP platform binary (macOS arm64); the Windows and Linux binaries are exercised by the documented-route and platform acceptance, not by this proof.
The RTX 5090 run used the candidate package in its qualification window before publication; the RTX 4090 run used the installed published package.
The RTX 4090 lane keeps its last two launches' logs, so the first restart's shutdown line is not retained; the turn after that restart reused its session's cache like the others.
Durability is shown for one short session per lane across graceful restarts. Crash restores after compaction and reclamation under quota pressure are EXP-074's.
